lessons: Start with high-stakes comparisons or physical thought experiments (e.g., cars vs dinosaurs, car crashes), as all videos successfully retained over 1.0 at 10% regardless of low relative start benchmarks.
Avoid overly dense technical explanations early on, as sudden drops occur around 11% to 25% when specific heavy metrics or secondary clauses are introduced.
Do not rely on countdowns since all analyzed videos had countdown=False, meaning retention relies entirely on pacing and narrative stakes rather than timer gimmicks.
Keep initial hooks punchy and tightly bounded, as longer introductory lines correlate with immediate viewer drop-off within the first 10-25% of the runtime.
worst_moment_types: Heavy technical specifications or definitions introduced too early (e.g., specific bone stress physics or jaw force numbers between 11% and 25%)
Mid-video pacing stalls where the explanation repeats or lingers on the mechanics rather than driving the narrative forward
best_hook_types: Counterintuitive physical questions (e.g., comparing dinosaur speed to cars, or why a crushing car saves lives)
Immersive identity-based scenarios ('Imagine you are a baby tyrannosaur')
